title: Generation suffix bleed-through in hosted routing causing customer eval overrun
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer ACME Analytics reported a reproducible increase in token counts and truncated JSON outputs during nightly evals after the runtime sampling-defaults change rolled last week. Symptoms only appear when requests route through hosted->private fallthrough paths (hosted routing layer -> private pool) and for streaming sessions longer than 512 tokens. The behavior manifests as extra comma/closing-brace tokens appended after expected stop sequences (a.k.a. 'suffix bleed-through'), which causes customer evals to exceed stop-token boundaries and fail strict JSON parsers. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a stable remediation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
reproduction_steps: Use ACME's nightly eval prompt set (attached link) against model redwood/gptxl-8k with sampling defaults from runtime-1.21
Enable streaming=true and send a 700-token context that includes an explicit stop sequence '\n--END--'
Route through hosted gateway with routing policy that fallbacks to ACME private pool
Observe extra tokens emitted after stop sequence in streaming chunks and in final output; compare with direct private pool run (no hosted gateway) which does not reproduce.
investigation_summary: Initial bisect shows change in 'sampling_defaults_tiered_switch' (runtime-1.21) altered sampling fallback order and introduced a subtle timing window where KV-cache flush and streaming chunk finalization race with stop-sequence enforcement in the routing layer. Repro across hardware types (A100/V100) but higher frequency on long-lived streaming sessions. Canary rollback of sampling defaults on a small subset eliminated the issue for affected customer.
root_cause: Routing-layer fallthrough path did not consistently apply the ingress-level stop_sequences bound when a streaming session's KV cache flush occurred mid-chunk during a model variant fallback. The sampling-default change changed chunk boundaries and increased probability of the race, leading to repeated tiny suffix tokens being generated and appended after the intended termination point.
mitigation_short_term: Enable per-customer ingress enforcement: host gateway will inject an enforced_stop_sequences param (server-side) for ACME to guarantee pre-tokenization termination
Deploy temporary runtime flag 'strict_stop_precedence' to Hosted routing fleet to prefer stop_sequence enforcement before any fallback or KV-cache flush
Coordinate a targeted rollback of sampling-defaults for ACME's hosted routing slice while remediation is built
Advise ACME to increase post-processing JSON tolerance as a short-lived workaround (already communicated)
Monitor token-rate and eval pass-rate dashboards (link in links section)
remediation_plan: Implement routing-layer contract change to carry canonical stop_sequences and enforce them at the final emission stage (runtime-1.22) with unit + integration tests
Add deterministic finalization step for streaming chunks that drains KV cache synchronously when stop_sequences are satisfied
Add regression tests using ACME's prompt set to the runtime test harness and CI
Ship release runtime-1.22 with canary rollout, gradual ramp, and customer-specific opt-in flag removed after 2 weeks of zero regressions
Postmortem and update runbook for similar routing fallthrough cases
